answers.rationale: Apply the schedule-specific buffer rule rather than a prior-night-arrival default. A 10:35 a.m. nonstop arrival leaves more than three hours before a 2:00 p.m. setup window, with no checked gear and clear weather; retain the two-night plan unless the setup moves earlier or equipment is added.

The checked scanner, post-check-in-only dock access, 40-minute drive, possible snow, and fixed 8:30 a.m. lab make the Monday arrival infeasible. Use the already-approved Sunday arrival to protect equipment handling and the first required activity.

Use the Monday nonstop because the required AV check is not until 2:30 p.m., the traveler is carry-on only, and weather is normal. The optional Sunday event does not justify a manager-noted extra hotel night; reassess only if the AV requirement moves materially earlier.

Use rideshare or Logan Express and walk the indoor conference connection. There is no equipment, offsite itinerary, or parking advantage supporting a rental, while the $58 nightly hotel parking makes a full-conference SUV disproportionate.
